completed_deductions: In a mixed (2,1) fiber with L(m) nonzero, specialization of the global volume relation forces the simple component to be collapsed. Otherwise its entire good projected line would hit the fixed vertical component.
Both component cylinders are distinct parallel affine planes in actual constant-affine good coordinates: q2B=(ell,Y), q1B=(ell,Y-1).
The actual good hyperplane ell=L(m) dot x_tr-kappa(m) has Eell in m^2 but nonzero, with E^2ell=0. It is not an E-invariant coordinate.
Canonical evaluation yields E-invariant F=ell-uEell and G=Y-uEY in A, exact component ideals q2=(F,G),q1=(F,G-1), and radical fiber (F,G(G-1)). No N-invariance or coordinate assertion follows.

Zero first normal N-action gives a constant quotient column and a unimodular polynomial row(p,q). The transverse binary quadratic class evaluated on(-q,p) is nonzero at every complex c, hence a nonzero constant.
With actual volume factor epsilon0=nu*p, weighted substitution v=y/p gives D*v=0 and D*c=2nu*A*v. Actual N^3F=N^3G=0 then implies p'''=q'''=0.
The polynomial row spans are, up to constant row and affine parameter changes, span{1},span{1,c},span{1,c^2},span{c,c^2+1}. This classifies indicated conormal data only.
A primitive intrinsic polynomial control N=-x^2*d_y+2y*d_c has the leading square-zero identity on c but N^2c=-2x^2 nonzero, blocking its promotion to the full action.
